_doc: ADR-031 (D-047 Parts 2-3, ruling 18; D-043 A8, B5). Civilization-wide generic UNIT FAMILIES. A family is a military ROLE that persists across Ages; each Age changes how the role is REALIZED (the identity). Civ VI upgrade lines and Age of Empires II unit lines are referenced for the PATTERN only (role persists, realization changes); no list or statistic is copied.

NO COMBAT STATISTICS. Attack, defence, range and movement are deferred to the military-capability architecture (D-043 A8; D-011 battle layer). Nothing here is read by any combat equation, because none exists.

line: the family's identities in Age order. identity.age is the first Age in which that identity is the family's realization. The family's realization at Age A is the identity with the greatest age <= A. A family with no identity at or below A does not exist yet at A.

MODERNIZATION (ruling 18 - automatic and free at Age transition): a unit of identity I in family F converts, when its owner enters Age A, to F's realization at A when that is a later identity than I. If F has no later identity by A the unit is PRESERVED unchanged until one exists. If F's line has ENDED (lineEndsAfterAge < A) the noSuccessor rule applies: preserve, or convert to the named generic family's realization at A. Location, ownership, experience and army membership are preserved.

equipment is DECLARATIVE: what a realization historically required. It is consumed by nothing - free modernization creates and destroys no conserved stock (law 1; CR-017 §4). realizedBy names the research.json unit entity whose knowledge requirement the identity corresponds to, where one exists; it gates nothing here.

GAP AUDIT (ADR-031 addendum). An Age at which a family's realization does not change is intentional, never an omission: the earlier identity remains the historically appropriate realization. Families absent before their first identity do not exist yet (no unit can hold them). light_infantry: scouts A1-A2, skirmishers A3-A4, light auxiliaries A5-A6, rangers A7-A8 (each a long-lived skirmish tradition). spear_anti_cavalry: begins A2 (composite-hafted spears); spearmen A2-A3 (bronze heads do not change the formation), phalanx A4-A5 (the Macedonian phalanx is Classical); line ends after A7 -> heavy_infantry. heavy_infantry: complete A1-A9 (A2 axe warriors close the founding warband's Neolithic gap). ranged_infantry: archers A2-A3, composite archers A4-A5. light_cavalry: begins A3 (no ridden horse before the Bronze Age); light horse A4-A5. heavy_cavalry: begins A3; chariots A3-A4; cuirassiers A7-A8 (cuirassier regiments served until 1914; no Industrial heavy-cavalry identity is invented). ranged_cavalry: begins A4 (steppe horse archery); horse archers A4-A5; line ends after A7 -> light_cavalry. siege: begins A4, complete A4-A9. naval_combat: begins A4 (the ram galley), complete A4-A9. naval_transport: shore craft A1-A2 (dugouts and hide boats remain Neolithic water transport), plank boats A3-A5. air and strategic_missile: begin A9 (no pre-industrial predecessor).

composition: army_formation = internal composition of an Army MobileAgent (B5: one banner, internal formations); mobile_agent = itself a MobileAgent token (fleets, air wings, strategic forces). Recruitment, movement, supply and Action Capacity are NOT implemented (later milestones).

M7 RECRUITMENT (ADR-055; unit charter 6.5-6.6, D-065). schema 2. Every identity declares a KNOWLEDGE GATE - realizedBy (a research.json entity), requires (an expression of research.json node ids, parsed by the research dialect; for identities with no realizedBy, and ANDed with it where both appear) or baseline (a research.json baseline capability: known from the start) - and RECRUITMENT DATA: personnel (adults transferred from the location's buckets by Ledger.Transfer), years (the recruitment time, read as the re-equipment duration: a rate x dtYears), inputs (goods by name and whole quantity, drawn from the empire stockpile and sunk by Ledger.Flow), optional building (a research.json building entity a completed structure at the location must realize), optional blockedBy (a named missing system or ruling; the identity is blocked while it is set). carrierCapable (air families: no / any / jet_deck) and jetDeck (carriers) form the one embark predicate (aviation-progression 9.1). A goods name must be in goods.json or in plannedGoods, which names the EC packet that will add it: an identity needing a planned good is BLOCKED and says which good and which packet. Quantities and personnel are PROVISIONAL bands, TUNE, never calibrated (charter 15.6).

TAXONOMY (charter 5.2-5.3, Q2 resolved 16.4; aviation-progression 3, 9.3): families 14 and 17-23 appended (D-065 R8-R10, Addendum 3: combat engineers, military supply and field medical are ABSTRACT military support capabilities, category B - not unit families; keys 13, 15 and 16 are withdrawn, unallocated and never reused; no prospector (R12: a one-shot action), sniper (R14: open, Q10) or trade/shipping family (R13); naval_transport (10) is unchanged pending an ADR-031 amendment); identities 101 -> reconnaissance (22), 907 -> submarines (18), 908 -> carriers (19, now its mainline), 1102 -> rotary_wing (20, now its mainline), 1104 -> unmanned_aircraft (21) - keys unchanged, never reused; a saved MilitaryUnits row of a rehomed identity is remapped at load (CanonicalSchema family migration). military_aircraft (1101) is the Flight I identity at A8; advanced piston aircraft (1105) the A9 mainline; jet fighters (1106) and stealth aircraft (1103) A9 branches. The identity Age is modernization metadata: recruitment never reads the Age (charter 6.5).

founding.basis: research.json baseline.basic_military ('Basic military (clubmen or equivalent)') is BASELINE: every founded Empire fields one warband at its capital. ADR-055 (Q7, unit charter 6.5 'nothing spawns'): with sim.json military on, its recruitment.personnel adults are drawn from the capital's adult buckets by Ledger.Transfer at founding (people stay conserved: they move into the formation's FormationPersonnel row); no goods are consumed; no combat exists (D-011 deferred). With the switch off it is the ADR-031 token, no personnel drawn.

families.name: Light Infantry / Skirmishers
families.role: Screening and skirmishing ahead of the main force (scouting is the reconnaissance agent, family 22).
families.historicalEmergence: Prehistoric hunting parties; formalized skirmishers in the Bronze and Iron Ages.

families.name: Spear / Anti-Cavalry Infantry
families.role: Close-order infantry that holds a line against mounted attack.
families.historicalEmergence: Composite-hafted spears (Neolithic); hoplite and phalanx formations; medieval pike.

noSuccessor.note: The socket bayonet made the pike obsolete: from the Industrial Age the anti-cavalry role is absorbed by line infantry.

line.name: Spearmen
line.reference: Civ VI Spearman; AoE II Spearman

line.name: Pikemen
line.reference: Civ VI Pikeman; AoE II Pikeman

families.name: Heavy Infantry / Line Infantry
families.role: The main battle infantry: shock and holding power in close combat, later the line of fire.
families.historicalEmergence: Founding warbands; Neolithic axe-armed warriors; bronze- and iron-armed heavy infantry; men-at-arms; musket and rifle infantry.

line.name: Warband
line.reference: Civ VI Warrior; AoE II Militia

line.name: Axe warriors
line.historicalEmergence: Neolithic farming-community fighters armed with ground- and polished-stone axes, adzes and mace-heads (LBK massacre sites such as Talheim, c. 5000 BC; later stone battle-axes)

line.name: Men-at-arms
line.reference: Civ VI Man-at-Arms; AoE II Man-at-Arms

families.name: Ranged Infantry
families.role: Infantry that fights at range: missile fire and, later, crew-served direct fire.
families.historicalEmergence: Slings and simple bows (Prehistoric); composite bows; crossbows and longbows; firearms.

branches.rule: The Medieval line branches: crossbowmen are the mainline realization; longbowmen are a regional branch (unit.longbowmen). Automatic conversion always follows the mainline, so it is deterministic.

line.name: Archers
line.reference: Civ VI Archer; AoE II Archer

line.name: Crossbowmen
line.reference: Civ VI Crossbowman; AoE II Crossbowman

families.name: Mounted Scout / Light Cavalry
families.role: Fast mounted reconnaissance, raiding and pursuit.
families.historicalEmergence: Horse domestication (Bronze Age); Iron Age riders; hussars; armoured cars.

line.name: Light horse
line.reference: Civ VI Horseman; AoE II Scout Cavalry

families.name: Heavy Cavalry
families.role: Shock troops: mounted (later armoured) units that break enemy lines.
families.historicalEmergence: Chariots (Bronze Age); cataphracts and knights; cuirassiers; tanks.

line.name: Knights
line.reference: Civ VI Knight; AoE II Knight

families.name: Ranged Cavalry
families.role: Mounted missile troops: harassment and fire on the move.
families.historicalEmergence: Horse archers (Iron Age steppe); mounted crossbowmen; dragoons.

noSuccessor.note: Mounted missile troops became carbine-armed light cavalry; from the Industrial Age the role is absorbed by the light-cavalry line.

families.name: Siege
families.role: Breaching fortifications and, later, indirect fire support.
families.historicalEmergence: Rams and towers (Iron Age); torsion engines; trebuchets; gunpowder artillery.

line.name: Rams and siege towers
line.historicalEmergence: the battering ram and siege tower
line.reference: Civ VI Battering Ram; AoE II Battering Ram

line.name: Trebuchets
line.reference: Civ VI Trebuchet; AoE II Trebuchet

families.name: Naval Combat
families.role: Fighting ships: control of rivers, coasts and seas.
families.historicalEmergence: Ram-armed war galleys (Iron Age); sailing warships; steam ironclads; modern surface navies (submarines and carriers are their own families).

families.name: Naval Transport
families.role: Moving armies and supplies over water.
families.historicalEmergence: Primitive shore-hugging craft (baseline); plank boats; seagoing and oceanic hulls; steam and motor transports.

line.name: Plank-built boats
line.historicalEmergence: plank-built hulls and the square sail

line.name: Oceanic transports
line.historicalEmergence: carracks and galleons (the oceanic transport class)

families.name: Air / Aviation
families.role: Air reconnaissance and air superiority, with a light-attack action (bombing is strike_aviation).
families.historicalEmergence: Military aviation in stages: powered flight (Flight I, Industrial Age), advanced aviation (Flight II), networked and stealth aviation (Flight III).

branches.rule: Flight II-III: jet fighters and stealth aircraft are recruited branches or re-equipment targets (D-065 R1), never modernization targets; automatic conversion follows the mainline (advanced piston aircraft).

line.name: Advanced piston aircraft
line.historicalEmergence: all-metal monoplane fighters and reconnaissance aircraft (Flight II)

line.name: Jet fighters
line.historicalEmergence: the first jet fighters (Flight II branch)

families.name: Specialized Modern Roles: Strategic Missile Forces
families.role: Long-range missile strike. A modern specialized role with no pre-industrial predecessor.
families.historicalEmergence: Rocketry (mid twentieth century).

recruitment.blockedBy: launch facility (building charter 5.23) and strategic governance (M10)
launch facility (building charter 5.23) and strategic governance (M10)

families.name: Air Defence
families.role: Deny the air over a formation or site.
families.historicalEmergence: Anti-aircraft artillery (First World War); radar-directed guns; surface-to-air missiles.

branches.rule: Surface-to-air missile batteries are a recruited branch, never a modernization target; radar direction is a capability of the AA identity once radar is known, not a new identity.

line.name: Anti-aircraft artillery
line.historicalEmergence: anti-aircraft guns (Flight I; a counter never precedes its threat)

families.name: Naval Raiders
families.role: Commerce raiding and coastal raids; avoids battle fleets.
families.historicalEmergence: Raiding galleys; privateers; commerce raiders.

noSuccessor.note: From the Modern Age commerce war passes to the submarine.

families.name: Submarines
families.role: Hidden sea denial and commerce war.
families.historicalEmergence: Diesel-electric submarines; nuclear submarines.

branches.rule: Nuclear submarines are a recruited branch (unit.nuclear_submarine); automatic conversion follows the mainline (diesel-electric submarines).

families.name: Carriers
families.role: A mobile air base: projects aviation.
families.historicalEmergence: Early aircraft carriers (Flight II); jet-capable fleet carriers (Flight III).

branches.rule: Jet-capable fleet carriers (angled deck, steam catapult) are a recruited branch; automatic conversion follows the mainline (aircraft carriers).

line.name: Jet-capable fleet carriers
line.historicalEmergence: angled-deck carriers with steam catapults (Flight III branch)

families.name: Rotary-Wing Aviation
families.role: Air mobility, close support and medevac.
families.historicalEmergence: Helicopters (mid twentieth century).

families.name: Unmanned Aircraft
families.role: Persistent reconnaissance, later precision strike.
families.historicalEmergence: Reconnaissance drones; combat drones.

branches.rule: Combat drones are a recruited branch (unit.combat_drone); automatic conversion follows the mainline (reconnaissance drones).

families.name: Reconnaissance
families.role: Reveal and keep current the knowledge of terrain, deposits and rivals (a MobileAgent, not a formation).
families.historicalEmergence: Hunter-scouts; survey patrols with map and compass.

line.name: Survey patrols
line.historicalEmergence: survey patrols with map, compass and survey

families.name: Strike Aviation
families.role: Bombing: tactical bombing of formations and works, then strategic bombing of production, infrastructure and depots.
families.historicalEmergence: Light bombers (Flight I); strategic bombers (Flight II); stealth bombers (Flight III).

branches.rule: Stealth bombers are a recruited branch or re-equipment target; automatic conversion follows the mainline (strategic bombers).
